value: lowest behavioural threshold about 0.6 µV/cm (peak-to-peak), found close to but not exactly at the electric-organ discharge fundamental frequency
method: food-rewarded conditioning: fish swam to a sine-wave field whose frequency was clamped to its own electric-organ discharge, thresholds interpolated at 70 % of trials responded to
conditions: Eigenmannia sp. imported from Colombia via a commercial dealer (9 fish, 11-20 cm, in the study; 3 fish, 16-20 cm, in the conditioning experiments), kept at 27 C, 12:12 L:D; water conductivity 100 µS/cm; 0.6 µV/cm was the lowest value in the study, from fish no. 1 at 0.99 and 1.01 times the discharge frequency; a threshold stimulus is about 1/3000 of the fish's own EOD field (3 mV/cm)

value: jamming avoidance threshold 1.27 µV/cm for a stimulus 1 Hz above the fish's resting discharge frequency, 25.07 µV/cm when the stimulus matched it exactly (about 20 dB higher)
eye: electroreceptors (whole animal, jamming avoidance response threshold)
method: jamming avoidance response: constant-frequency sine-wave stimulus not clamped to the discharge, set at DF 0, -1 or +1 Hz from the resting discharge frequency; fish held in a shelter behind plastic mesh, discharge frequency counted; threshold = lowest intensity giving a significant shift from resting frequency within 40-60 s of onset (paired t-test, P<0.01); stimulus rise and fall 400 ms
conditions: Eigenmannia sp., N=6 juveniles 11 cm long; water conductivity 100 µS/cm; threshold depended significantly on DF (F=15.154, P<0.0003, d.f.=17), DF 0 above both -1 and +1 Hz, no difference between -1 and +1 Hz; the threshold rise at frequency identity was larger in this unclamped JAR test (up to 32 dB, mean 20 dB) than in the food-rewarded, frequency-clamped detection experiments (up to 15 dB, mean 13 dB), which the authors relate to the longer stimulus rise time (400 ms against 35 ms)

value: most sensitive neural response at 80 kHz, threshold 54.9 dB SPL (mean, s.e. 1.0)
eye: tympanal ear; A1 receptor cell in the auditory nerve
method: extracellular recording from the tympanal nerve with ultrasonic pulses (criterion: two or more spikes in at least 8 of 10 stimuli); laser Doppler vibrometry of the tympanal membrane from 50 to 300 kHz at 90 dB SPL
conditions: laboratory greater wax moths, 20 moths for the nerve thresholds (10 of each sex); only the A1 cell was analysed; laser vibrometry peaks were about 90-95 kHz in females and 125 kHz in males, a sex difference the authors found not significant
